decisionMeaning: MKT-03. This manifest declares, for every sold connector, the pre-prompt / pre-tool / post-tool-output / pre-delivery-response / model-stream / network interception points, the tamper posture and the outcome of the plugin-disabled, crashed, offline and large-binary-response conditions. A status of `enforced` requires a named real-host acceptance record in the row evidence. The records under docs/evidence/real-host/ are written by `pnpm test:e2e:real-host`: the real, unmodified host binary (Claude Code 2.1.282, Codex CLI 0.141.0, OpenCode 1.18.32, OpenClaw 2026.9.6) runs one non-interactive turn per scenario against a scripted loopback mock model, with AIDR installed from the development build in a disposable HOME on linux/x64. A row is `enforced` only where such a record proves the point for that host version on that platform and the support matrix sells the point. Since 2026-09-30 the support matrix sells pre-prompt for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and OpenClaw and OpenClaw's pre-model post-tool-output (additionalInterceptionPoints), so those rows are `enforced` on their records; OpenClaw's pre-delivery-response stays `declared-not-proven` because no record exercises channel delivery. Cursor and VS Code have no record (their hosts could not be installed in the evidence environment), and no record covers Windows, macOS, arm64, a signed commercial artefact or a real model, so the decision stays NO-GO.

limitations: Prompt protection (secrets block, personal data warns by default) inspects the prompt text only; a hook process killed before it answers cannot block, which is a Claude Code host limitation.

Real-host acceptance: Claude Code 2.1.282 on linux/x64 stopped a prompt carrying a GitHub token at UserPromptSubmit before any model request, and the audit entry records kinds only (scripted mock model, docs/evidence/real-host/claude-code.json). Other host versions and platforms are not covered.

Sold since 2026-09-30 (deploy/native/support-matrix.json additionalInterceptionPoints). `enforced` rests on that one real-host record only: Claude Code 2.1.282 (`claude -p`), linux/x64, the development build and a scripted mock model. Windows, macOS, arm64, a signed commercial artefact, a real model and other host versions are not covered.

Real-host acceptance covers Claude Code 2.1.282 on linux/x64 with a scripted mock model: a curl-pipe-to-shell Bash call and a Read of a private-key canary were refused with no side effect and nothing of the canary reached the model, a benign call ran, and the same malicious call ran when the plugin was absent (docs/evidence/real-host/claude-code.json). Other host versions, platforms and real-model turns are not covered.

The hook always exits 0. A hook process killed before it writes a verdict fails open on this host (see failureConditions crashed-hook); the connector's own inspection deadline was observed to deny instead.
An `ask` verdict was observed only in non-interactive `-p` mode, where the host refuses the call; the interactive approval dialog is not exercised.
The host boundary is PostToolUse, so the tool has already executed; this is a tool-result boundary and not a refusal of the action.
Only the updatedToolOutput replacement path is claimed; a PostToolUse block without replacement still exposes the original result to the model.

Real-host acceptance: on Claude Code 2.1.282 a Bash result carrying a GitHub token reached the model only as AIDR's quarantine notice (docs/evidence/real-host/claude-code.json). That run found and fixed a Bash result-shape mismatch (`noOutputExpected`); MCP and other tool result shapes are not host-accepted.
